football_evidence.question: Can Baylor’s pass rush get to Isaiah Marshall?
football_evidence.assessment: EdgeDesk’s number is 3.0 points closer to Kansas than the line, and EdgeDesk cannot account for most of that: its own breakdown accounts for about 1.0 of the 3.0 points. The measured football evidence leans toward Baylor, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.
supporting: When Kansas has the ball (big plays through the air): Kansas’ offense turns 15.8% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Baylor’s defense gives up explosive gains on 10.0% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).
When Baylor has the ball (the red zone): Baylor’s offense succeeds on 30.7% of its red-zone plays, and Kansas’ defense allows success on 37.6% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
DJ Lagway has completed 91 of 185 passes (49.2%) for 1,098 yards, 5.9 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in four games for Baylor, and has been sacked on 8 of 193 dropbacks.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Kansas’ offensive line No. 35 nationally and Baylor’s No. 85.
contradicting: When Kansas has the ball (big plays on the ground): Kansas’ offense turns 5.6% of its runs into explosive gains, and Baylor’s defense gives up explosive gains on 3.4% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Kansas has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Kansas’ offense has allowed a sack on 3.3% of its dropbacks, and Baylor’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Kansas has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Kansas’ offense averages 5.2 yards per carry, and Baylor’s defense allows 3.8 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Kansas has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Kansas’ offense is stopped at or behind the line on 15.2% of its runs, and Baylor’s defense stops 24.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
quarterbacks: Isaiah Marshall has completed 88 of 167 passes (52.7%) for 1,338 yards, 8.0 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in six games for Kansas, and has been sacked on 6 of 173 dropbacks.
DJ Lagway has completed 91 of 185 passes (49.2%) for 1,098 yards, 5.9 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in four games for Baylor, and has been sacked on 8 of 193 dropbacks.
Nate Bennett has completed 45 of 61 passes (73.8%) for 566 yards, 9.3 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in three games for Baylor, and has been sacked on 4 of 65 dropbacks.
